name: AI Calculators and Interactive Decision Tools
blurb: Six interactive estimators for the questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment. Each shows its own arithmetic and states what it excludes.

reading.body:
Six interactive estimators cover the six questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment.

The set treats compute, power, and cost as equally load-bearing. GPU memory and context window fit measure whether a model can run at all, while token and training cost measure whether it can run affordably. Energy and carbon make the grid constraint explicit in the same viability check as return on investment.

Each estimator shows its own arithmetic and states what it excludes, so the numbers are meant to be auditable rather than black-box. No worked examples or numeric results are included, only the list of six tools. It does not say how the estimators interact or which one dominates in practice.
